sources.location: https://ftp.pride.ebi.ac.uk/pride/data/archive/2025/03/PXD061360/LC-MS_files.zip (central directory read by HTTP range request; 24 .d folders)

claims.evidence: The 24 Bruker .d folders in LC-MS_files.zip are the same 24 experiments listed in mqpar.xml. The archive is one zip, so .d names come from inside it.

N = leading number of the file name; data processing protocol refers to samples 1,4,7,8,10,12,13,14,16,17,19,20,21,22,23,24. Source names are our labels; one run per sample, mapping inferred from file names.
PRIDE organism NEWT:9606 and protocol: human muscle mitochondria.
Mitochondria isolated from homogenised muscle tissue.
Sample protocol: isolated from healthy volunteers.
Healthy volunteers (adult inferred; ages not given).
No per-sample demographics in the deposit; no publication listed.
PRIDE instruments field and protocol (nanoElute + timsTOF fleX).
mqpar enzymes Trypsin/P, MaxMissedCleavages 2. Digestion reagent is not named in PRIDE prose.

claims.value: Carbamidomethyl (C) fixed; Oxidation (M), Acetyl (Protein N-term) variable

claims.evidence: mqpar mainSearchTol 10 ppm; TOF msmsParams MatchTolerance 25 ppm.
Assumed: standard for timsTOF PASEF; not stated in the deposit.

limitations: No publication is listed; protocol only. Sample numbers and groups cannot be tied to any clinical or biochemical variable.

24 .d runs deposited and searched, but the protocol says only 16 samples (1,4,7,8,10,12,13,14,16,17,19,20,21,22,23,24) are used in the project. Samples 31-34 and 41-44 are annotated with the same generic values; their identity is not described.
Leading file number is taken to be the sample number; not stated explicitly.
Trypsin comes from the MaxQuant search enzyme, not from protocol prose (reconcile flagged this). Dissociation CID is assumed.
No factor value column: no experimental comparison is described.
Raw files are inside one 134 GB zip; comment[data file] uses the .d folder names. Instrument was not verified from analysis.tdf.
